distinguishing_features: Engineered textured or seeded heat-exchanger surfaces intentionally initiate ice nucleation at the wall rather than suppressing wall nucleation by changing the operating setpoint.
Flow is adjusted to trigger nucleation at low supercooling and promote a controlled ice front.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce uncontrolled ice formation and consequent solute entrapment during juice freeze-concentration.
parsed.viable_reason: Heterogeneous nucleation at a surface is physically plausible and testable, although the stated supercooling thresholds and uniform-front results are not established by the proposal.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: A skilled engineer seeking to control stochastic freezing could routinely use known heterogeneous nucleation sites to initiate ice at a chosen surface, particularly when the closest art already addresses nucleation at heat-transfer walls.
